- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3%.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (mean reversion signal), increase forecast by 1–2% to align with momentum.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 1–2% in next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period prices; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
